title: All-Edges Sparse Triangle below m^{4/3} on balanced instances
credit: Alman, Vassilevska Williams 2026, arXiv:2610.06783, Sec. 6; Patrascu, STOC 2010
premise_risks: arXiv:2610.06783 (Alman-Vassilevska Williams, Oct 2026, unrefereed): the claim that lopsided AE-Sparse-Triangle (and 3SUM, APSP) are now truly subquadratic/subcubic, and that balanced instances remain open, i.e. the reason this is the live question and that 3SUM-based m^{4/3} hardness has fallen.
plain: Solve All-Edges Sparse Triangle (for each of m edges, report whether it is in a triangle) in O(m^{4/3-eps}) time on general (balanced) sparse graphs, or derive an m^{4/3-o(1)} lower bound from a hypothesis that survives AVW (e.g. 4SUM, OV/SETH, or combinatorial BMM).
math: Model: word-RAM with Θ(log N)-bit words. Let G be a tripartite graph on parts A, B, C with |A|=|B|=|C|=N, m=Θ(N^{3/2}) edges and maximum degree O(√N). Is there a (possibly randomized) algorithm that, for every edge of every such G, decides whether that edge lies in a triangle, in time O(m^{4/3-ε}) for some fixed ε>0? (The alternative 'show that such an algorithm refutes a hypothesis still standing after AVW' is a separate, conditional-hardness question and should be posed as its own problem with a named hypothesis, e.g. 4SUM or OV.)
lean_gap: Not formalized: needs a word-RAM model with time bounds (and, for the alternative, fine-grained reductions), absent from Mathlib.
